title: Species & areas III: status, trafficking, recovery

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about pangolins:
1. They are the only mammals whose bodies are fully covered in keratin scales.
2. The Indian pangolin is IUCN Endangered, whereas the Chinese pangolin, found in Assam and the eastern Himalayas, is Critically Endangered.
3. The Himalayan pangolin (Manis aurita) has been recognised as a species distinct from the Indian pangolin.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 names the wrong parent: the Himalayan pangolin was confirmed as a species separate from the Chinese pangolin (Manis pentadactyla), the lineages having split about 1.8 million years ago. Both Indian species are in Schedule I of the WPA and CITES Appendix I, and 'DNA maps' are being used to trace trafficking hubs.
questions.s: SPP notes D (CA 2026, Vision IAS pp. 67-68, 85-86)

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Species : IUCN status
1. Indian soft-shell turtle : Endangered
2. Indian pangolin : Critically Endangered
3. Southern elephant seal : Endangered
4. Asiatic cheetah : Critically Endangered
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Only pairs 1 and 4 are correct. The Indian pangolin is Endangered (the Chinese pangolin is the Critically Endangered one), and the southern elephant seal was moved to Vulnerable from Least Concern because of avian influenza. The emperor penguin and the Antarctic fur seal were raised to Endangered, with climate change the driver.
questions.s: SPP notes D (CA 2026, Vision IAS pp. 71-72, 85-86)

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the Great Indian Bustard is correct?
o: It is Critically Endangered on the IUCN Red List, in Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 and in CITES Appendix I
It is the State bird of Gujarat and survives mainly in the Western Ghats
It is a forest-canopy bird that feeds mainly on fruit
It is classed Endangered by the IUCN and is found mainly in the Sundarbans
questions.e: The Great Indian Bustard is an agro-grassland bird of Rajasthan, Gujarat, Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh, and Rajasthan's State bird. The WII's status report puts the Thar population at 130 plus or minus 21, stable since 2017-18, with Jaisalmer as the last stronghold. Overhead power lines, solar plants, farm fencing, feral dogs and invasive Prosopis juliflora are the main threats.
questions.s: SPP notes D (CA Jul 2026, Vision IAS p. 68)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the rewilding of the Great Indian Bustard:
1. The first captive-bred birds were released in Desert National Park, near Jaisalmer.
2. Project GIB eggs were incubated at Sam and Ramdevra, giving 98 captive-bred birds.
3. The Supreme Court accepted expert-panel priority areas of 14,013 sq km in Rajasthan and 740 sq km in Gujarat.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: All three are correct. Two males were released first, with 11 more earmarked; the release protocol uses anti-imprinting rewilding aviaries at 3-4 months and satellite transmitters reporting thrice daily. The Court asked for critical power lines to be undergrounded in 2027-28. The population fell from 1,260-1,400 in the early 1970s to about 150, roughly 130 of them in Rajasthan.
questions.s: SPP notes D (CA Sept 2026, Shankar pp. 94-95)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about snow leopards in India:
1. The first nationwide assessment (2019-2023) estimated 718 snow leopards, of which Ladakh had 477.
2. Uttarakhand has more snow leopards than Ladakh.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. Ladakh's 477 is the highest and Uttarakhand's 124 is a distant second. SPAI 2.0 was launched in Wildlife Week 2025, and Kibber village women work with the Nature Conservation Foundation and the Snow Leopard Trust. The snow leopard is one of the seven species of the International Big Cat Alliance.
questions.s: SPP notes B (CA Jan and Aug 2026, Shankar)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about river dolphins and Project Dolphin:
1. Project Dolphin was launched on 15 August 2021.
2. The second range-wide estimation was launched in January 2026 from Patna.
3. The 2021-23 survey estimated 3,627 river dolphins.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: None is correct. Project Dolphin was launched on 15 August 2020 under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme 'Development of Wildlife Habitats'; the second estimation began in January 2026 from Bijnor; and the 2021-23 survey estimated 6,327 riverine dolphins. The new round adds the Irrawaddy dolphin (Sundarbans and Odisha) to the Gangetic and Indus river dolphins.
questions.s: SPP notes B (CA Jan 2026, Shankar pp. 7-8; Vision IAS pp. 76-77)

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Item : Detail
1. Vikramshila Gangetic Dolphin Sanctuary : Bihar
2. India's first Dugong Conservation Reserve : Gulf of Kachchh
3. Dolphin Conservation Zone : Chambal River
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Only pairs 1 and 3 are correct. The Dugong Conservation Reserve is in Palk Bay, Tamil Nadu; WII's 2026 estimate is 270 dugongs, 158 in Palk Bay and 112 in the Gulf of Mannar. River dolphins (superfamily Platanistoidea) are functionally blind, navigate by echolocation and indicate river health.
questions.s: SPP notes B, D (CA 2026, Vision IAS pp. 76-77; Shankar pp. 95-97)

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the Antarctic species reassessed by the IUCN is not correct?
o: The emperor penguin is now Endangered, with climate change the driver
The Antarctic fur seal is now Endangered, with climate change the driver
The emperor penguin is the smallest of the 18 penguin species
The southern elephant seal is now Vulnerable, with bird flu the driver
questions.e: The emperor penguin is the largest, not the smallest, of the 18 penguin species. It moved to Endangered from Near Threatened, the fur seal to Endangered from Least Concern, and the southern elephant seal, the largest seal, to Vulnerable from Least Concern, after avian influenza reached it. Polar species act as climate sentinels and show zoonotic spill-over into wildlife.
questions.s: SPP notes D (CA 2026, Vision IAS pp. 71-72)

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of camel breed and State is correctly matched?
questions.e: Kharai is a Gujarat breed (along with Kutchi). Malvi is named after the Malwa region of Madhya Pradesh; it is the smallest recognised breed, white, endangered in the 2019 livestock census, and a breeding programme was launched for it. Jalori is from Rajasthan, as are Bikaneri, Jaisalmeri, Marwari and Mewari; Mewati spans Rajasthan and Haryana. India recognises nine breeds.
questions.s: SPP notes D (CA Jul 2026, Vision IAS p. 68)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Bactrian camel:
1. India has about 300-400 of them, all in the Nubra Valley of Ladakh.
2. It has a single hump that stores fat.
3. The domesticated Bactrian camel and the wild Bactrian camel are the same species.
4. Two Bactrian camels marched in the 2025 Republic Day Parade.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. The Bactrian camel has two humps and tolerates temperatures from -30 to 40 degrees C. The domesticated animal (Camelus bactrianus) is not threatened, while the wild Bactrian camel (Camelus ferus) is a separate, threatened species; the source labels it Endangered. The camels marched in the 2026 Republic Day Parade.
questions.s: SPP notes D (CA Jan 2026, Vision IAS p. 77)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Prosopis juliflora:
1. It is native to India and was domesticated by the British in the 1920s.
2. It is a phreatophyte whose deep roots draw water from below the water table.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct. The tree is native to Mexico, was brought in by the British in the 1920s to green Delhi and by the Gujarat Forest Department in 1961, and it deepens hydrological drought and displaces native plants. It will be feedstock for India's first green methanol plant, intended for ocean-going ships, and its removal is part of the GIB habitat plan. IUCN lists it as Least Concern.
questions.s: SPP notes D (CA 2026, Vision IAS p. 86)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about species recovery in India:
1. The Jatayu Conservation Breeding Centre at Pinjore was set up by the BNHS with the Haryana government.
2. India's first Dugong Conservation Reserve is in the Gulf of Kachchh.
3. The Nilgiri Tahr count fell from 1,364 in 2025 to 1,303 in 2026.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. The Dugong Conservation Reserve is in Palk Bay, Tamil Nadu, and Project Nilgiri Tahr's count rose from 1,303 (2025) to 1,364 (2026). Vultures recovered after the diclofenac ban: Madhya Pradesh's census went from 8,397 (2019) to 12,981 (2025). Asiatic lions rose from 674 (2020) to 891 (2025).
questions.s: SPP notes D (CA Sept 2026, Shankar pp. 95-97)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: River dolphins are regarded as indicator species of river health.
Statement-II: River dolphins are functionally blind and navigate by echolocation.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I. Dolphins indicate river health because, as apex predators, their numbers track fish, water quality and flow, and because they need deep, continuous channels; echolocation is simply how they sense their surroundings. Conservation steps include the Vikramshila sanctuary in Bihar, the Chambal conservation zone and satellite-tagging of the Ganges river dolphin.
questions.s: SPP notes B (CA Jan 2026, Vision IAS pp. 76-77)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The emperor penguin was moved to Endangered mainly because of avian influenza.
Statement-II: The southern elephant seal was moved to Vulnerable because bird flu reached it.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct. Climate change is the driver for the emperor penguin and the Antarctic fur seal, both now Endangered, while avian influenza is blamed for the southern elephant seal's move to Vulnerable. The pattern illustrates two different pressures on polar species: warming of habitat and zoonotic spill-over.
questions.s: SPP notes D (CA 2026, Vision IAS pp. 71-72)

questions.q:
Which of the following species are listed in Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 and in CITES Appendix I, according to the notes?
1. Indian soft-shell turtle
2. Indian pangolin
3. Chinese pangolin
4. Jeypore ground gecko
questions.e: The turtle and both pangolins carry Schedule I and Appendix I. The Jeypore ground gecko is Schedule I but in CITES Appendix II, and is IUCN Endangered. Appendix I bars commercial trade in wild-caught specimens, whereas Appendix II regulates trade through permits (static). Presumed extinct for 130 years, the gecko was rediscovered in Koraput in 2010.
questions.s: SPP notes D (CA 2026, Vision IAS p. 85; Recitals pp. 103-104)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about migratory species:
1. The Global Initiative on the Taking of Migratory Species was launched at CMS COP15 in Quito, Ecuador, in March 2026.
2. According to the State of the World's Migratory Species report 2024, illegal or unsustainable taking threatens about 7% of the 1,200 CMS-listed species.
3. The CMS interim report of 2026 found that about 24% of listed species have declining populations and nearly 49% are globally threatened.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: None is correct. COP15 was held at Campo Grande, Brazil; taking threatens 70% of the 1,200 listed species; and nearly 49% are declining while about 24% are globally threatened. The initiative has four focus areas: data and monitoring, legal and policy frameworks, community engagement and awareness, and supports Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework goals, with partners such as UNEP-WCMC, WWF and TRAFFIC. CMS is the Bonn Convention (1979, static).
questions.s: SPP notes D (CA 2026, Vision IAS pp. 55, 72)
